items.title: George P. Fleming Interview, 1984-10-06
items.q: I'd go next door and hear George Lewis and Jim Robinson. Then I'd sit in there for a while

ctx.x: So he would have his program and they always had sheet music. They were good musicians and he would teach me, he would show me how to do this. Well, you do this and you play this and you play that. I'll play it down once and I had a goodie at that time and then he would play it down and he'd show me how to play and through my ear and my little spelling and I'd begin to get familiar with music. And it was there, it was shortly, I used to go down there every night and then I'd go next door and hear George Lewis and…

You said they had sheet music, you know, all those bands that we hear now, you know, they made these records in the late, in the 60s, the late 50s, 60s, 70s, the kind of preservation hall bands. Were they playing the same kind of music then or was it much more arranged?
